clue.text: Preferred sort of countryside spin, out touring round lake

indicators.note: round says the shuffled letters go around the next piece
touring suggests the letters wandering about, so the words spin and out are jumbled

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone talks of a drive spinning out round a lake through the countryside they prefer.
explanation.definitionFit: Countryside people prefer is untouched and natural, left unspoilt by development.

clue.text: 12's first sex client

definitions.meaning: 12 is MILTON; the poet Milton's first name was ...
a prostitute's customer is called a ... in slang

explanation.walkthrough: 12 points to the 12-across answer, so '12's first' means the first name of the poet Milton.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls a prostitute's customer a john, and the poet Milton was christened John.

clue.text: Carrier to stick around old George?

indicators.note: around says the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: to stick something is to pin it
Geo. is an old written abbreviation of the name George

explanation.surface: Asks whether a carrier will stick around for an old man named George.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrier pigeon delivers messages, so the bird is known as a carrier.

clue.text: Made to reduce one's workload

parts.note: to make ... into a task is to reduce how much remains, so the clue hints at the word completing 'made ...'

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a description of someone forced to cut their work, but it is the phrase 'made inroads', which is what you do when your workload shrinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Making inroads into a job means making progress that eats into what is left to do.

clue.text: Continental-style leaf-roof houses

indicators.note: houses means the following words contain the letters within them

explanation.surface: Describes a European look of roofs thatched with leaves on houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continental' suggests Europe, but the continent meant is Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Afro as a prefix means African, so this is a style from the African continent.

clue.text: Sufficient income to get by, one set about being a raver

parts.note: earning a living means having enough to get by on
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: about signals turning the next word round

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: Someone with enough to live on sets about partying hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Living it up means partying and enjoying oneself lavishly, as a raver does.

clue.text: Cut out new diet eaten by much reduced chap

indicators.note: eaten by says the jumbled letters go inside the short name

parts.note: Ed is a shortened form of a man's name like Edward, cut down a lot

indicators.note: made out new means rearranged, signalling the letters of diet shuffled

explanation.surface: A man on a new diet is cutting things out and shrinking a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out new' is the anagram signal; 'much reduced' tells you the chap's name is cut right down to two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A text that has been cut down for length or content has been edited.

clue.text: Going cool, feeling topless

parts.note: in means fashionable or cool

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: an emotion is a feeling

explanation.surface: Someone goes along feeling cool without a top on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in motion is moving, which is what going means here.

clue.text: Overheated dancer's first to grab one

indicators.note: to grab means the dancer's name takes hold of the next letter

parts.note: the dancer meant is Fred Astaire
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: The first dancer to grab a partner gets hot and bothered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is a link here, not a pick: the dancer is Fred Astaire, who 'grabs' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for overheated or burnt out by heat is fried, as in a fried circuit.

clue.text: See 23
Web fraud? Excludes taking in society, as exemplified by 12 9 17 and 2 15 26 down 22

parts.note: an e-con is an online scam, a con done electronically

indicators.note: taking in means the word encloses the next piece

parts.note: to exclude something is to omit it

explanation.surface: Asks whether online fraud keeps certain societies out, citing a list of cross-references.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers spell out Milton Friedman and John Maynard Keynes from the grid's linked lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton Friedman and John Maynard Keynes were two of the most influential economic thinkers, so they exemplify this profession.

clue.text: Fish roe covering vital US politician backing town

parts.note: milt is the soft roe of a male fish
on can mean covering, as a lid is on a pot
key means crucial or vital

indicators.note: backing signals that the word runs in reverse

parts.note: Sen. abbreviates senator, a US politician

explanation.surface: Fish roe is draped over a key American senator who supports a town.
explanation.walkthrough: MILTON KEYNES is a new town in Buckinghamshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large planned town in England, built from the 1960s onward.

clue.text: Filled with petrol, revved, drove off and got there in no time

indicators.note: filled with means the outer word holds the next piece inside

parts.note: in golf you drive off from the tee, so teed off means drove off

indicators.note: revved suggests an engine churning, so the letters of petrol are jumbled

explanation.surface: A car fills up, revs and drives off as if arriving instantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drove off' looks like part of the motoring picture, but it is the golfer's teeing off; 'revved' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be teleported is to travel instantly from one place to another, as in science fiction.

clue.text: Dodgems distributed round third of fair — not for ordinary folk

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters enclose the next piece
distributed suggests spreading the letters around in a new order
third of picks out the third letter of the word fair

explanation.surface: Dodgem cars are spread around a fairground, ride not meant for ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: DEMIGODS are half-divine, so they stand above ordinary folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Demigods are half-gods, beings set apart from and above ordinary mortals.

clue.text: Upside-down tuber's blossom

indicators.note: in a down clue upside-down means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a yam is a starchy tuber

explanation.surface: A tuber turned upside down sprouts a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn flowers are known as may, the blossom of late spring.

clue.text: Temperature taken by measurement with voided mercury ruler

indicators.note: taken by means the letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: a pole is an old unit of length

indicators.note: voided means emptied, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A temperature reading is taken with a mercury instrument used as a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' suggests a measuring stick, fitting the thermometer picture, but it means a king: Ptolemy was the name of Egypt's Greek pharaohs.
explanation.definitionFit: Several kings of Egypt bore this name, so it names a ruler.

clue.text: Unnatural as an oversexed female with electronic bottom

indicators.note: bottom means the letter goes at the foot of this down entry

parts.note: a woman obsessed with men is called man-mad

explanation.surface: Something artificial is pictured as a lusty woman with an electronic rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Artificial things are made by people rather than nature.

clue.text: Sally, with "everything out" — loose wear, produces a heartbeat moment

indicators.note: out means those letters are taken away from the name

parts.note: all means everything
a stole is a loose wrap worn over the shoulders

explanation.surface: Sally strips everything off except a loose wrap, and hearts skip a beat.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ALL from SALLY leaves SY.
explanation.definitionFit: Systole is the phase of the heartbeat when the heart muscle contracts.

clue.text: Which is unlikely means of capturing a crowd scene on film?

definitions.meaning: a bet or outcome with little chance of success

definitions.text: means of capturing a crowd scene on film?
definitions.meaning: a camera shot taken from far away, showing a wide scene

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both an improbable chance and a wide camera shot from a distance.

clue.text: An elemental form of pies — too flaky

indicators.note: flaky pastry crumbles, so the letters of pies and too break up and reform

explanation.surface: Describes a pie whose crust is too flaky to hold its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotope is one form of a chemical element, differing in neutron count.

clue.text: Kiss ground, holding breath, as sporty types are into?

indicators.note: holding means the jumbled letters wrap round the next piece
ground means crushed, so the letters of kiss are broken up

parts.note: a pant is a short gasping breath

explanation.surface: Sporty types kiss the ground, out of breath, after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' turns KISS into SKIS, which holds PANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski pants are trousers that skiers and sporty people put on, so they get into them.

clue.text: See 12
Need the help of upended wild horse with no tail

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of upended running out of order
with no tail means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a pony is a small horse

explanation.surface: A wild horse, tail lost, turns everything upside down and needs help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upended' looks like a reversal signal, but it is the anagram fodder, rearranged by 'wild' to give DEPENDU.
explanation.definitionFit: To rely on someone is to need their help.

clue.text: Frank's awful, heartless, malign woman

parts.note: dire means dreadful or awful

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: cat is slang for a spiteful woman

explanation.surface: Frank calls someone an awful, cruel, spiteful woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid, straightforward speech is direct speech.

clue.text: Instrument of geometry replaced in short time

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the short time

parts.note: hr is short for hour, a time

indicators.note: replaced means the letters of geometry are put back in another order

explanation.surface: A geometry instrument is swapped for another in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' is the anagram signal; 'short time' is the usual abbreviation for an hour, which wraps the scrambled word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hygrometer is a device for measuring the humidity of the air.

clue.text: See 17
War artist's Nuclear Residue

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Names a war painter's subject as nuclear fallout.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Nash was a British official war artist in both world wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Nash painted scenes of the First and Second World War battlefields as an official war artist.

clue.text: Sort of balm used in lunar descent

indicators.note: used in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A soothing balm is applied during a moon landing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spikenard, or nard, is an aromatic ointment from an ancient plant.

clue.text: Be an editor, tremendously content!

indicators.note: content means the letters contained within the word

explanation.surface: An editor declares themselves tremendously happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like an adjective meaning happy; it is the noun, what the word holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct and improve a text is the work an editor does.

clue.text: Old rogue, sanctimonious one, coming in to sing a love ballad?

parts.note: pi is slang for sanctimonious, short for pious

indicators.note: coming in means the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: to croon is to sing softly and sentimentally
a means one

explanation.surface: A pious old rogue joins in to sing a love ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: Picaroon is an archaic word for a rogue, rascal or pirate.
